This vignette benchmarks JointODE fitting performance across different data
sizes and parallelization settings.

## Setup

```{r load}
library(JointODE)
library(ggplot2)
```

## Benchmark Helper

```{r helper}
default_longitudinal <- list(
  xi = c(mean = 0.4, sd = 0.1),
  period = c(mean = 6, sd = 0.1),
  excitation = list(offset = 0.0, covariates = c(x1 = 0.5, x2 = -0.45)),
  initial = list(
    offset = c(biomarker = -0.5, velocity = -0.1),
    covariates = list(
      biomarker = c(x1 = 0.08, x2 = -0.06),
      velocity = c(x1 = 0.25, x2 = -0.2)
    )
  ),
  error_sd = 0.1,
  n_measurements = 100
)

bench_fit <- function(n_subjects, n_measurements, parallel, n_cores = 0,
                      maxit = 30, seed = 42) {
  long_config <- default_longitudinal
  long_config$n_measurements <- n_measurements

  sim <- simulate(
    n_subjects = n_subjects,
    longitudinal = long_config,
    seed = seed
  )

  longitudinal_data <- sim$longitudinal_data[
    , c("id", "time", "observed", "x1", "x2")
  ]
  survival_data <- sim$survival_data

  elapsed <- system.time({
    fit <- JointODE(
      longitudinal_formula = observed ~ biomarker + velocity + x1 + x2 +
        (biomarker + velocity | id),
      survival_formula = Surv(time, status) ~ w1 + w2,
      longitudinal_data = longitudinal_data,
      survival_data = survival_data,
      control = list(
        maxit = maxit,
        parallel = parallel,
        n_cores = n_cores,
        atol = 1e-3
      )
    )
  })[["elapsed"]]

  data.frame(
    n_subjects = n_subjects,
    n_measurements = n_measurements,
    n_obs = nrow(longitudinal_data),
    parallel = parallel,
    n_cores = if (parallel) {
      if (n_cores == 0) parallel::detectCores() else n_cores
    } else {
      1L
    },
    maxit = maxit,
    iterations = fit$convergence$em_iterations,
    converged = fit$convergence$converged,
    elapsed = elapsed,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}
```

## 1. Scaling with Data Size (Sequential)

Fix `maxit = 30` to compare raw per-iteration cost across data sizes.

```{r bench-size}
size_configs <- list(
  list(n = 100, m = 50),
  list(n = 150, m = 80),
  list(n = 200, m = 100)
)

results_size <- do.call(rbind, lapply(size_configs, function(cfg) {
  bench_fit(cfg$n, cfg$m, parallel = FALSE)
}))

results_size$time_per_iter <- results_size$elapsed / results_size$iterations
knitr::kable(
  results_size[, c("n_subjects", "n_measurements", "n_obs",
                    "iterations", "elapsed", "time_per_iter")],
  digits = 2,
  col.names = c("Subjects", "Measurements", "Total Obs",
                "Iterations", "Time (s)", "s/iter"),
  caption = "Sequential performance by data size (maxit = 30)"
)
```

## 2. Parallel Scaling

Compare sequential vs parallel (2, 4, and all cores) on medium-sized data.

```{r bench-parallel}
n_available <- parallel::detectCores()

parallel_configs <- list(
  list(parallel = FALSE, n_cores = 0),
  list(parallel = TRUE,  n_cores = 2)
)
if (n_available >= 4) {
  parallel_configs <- c(parallel_configs, list(
    list(parallel = TRUE, n_cores = 4)
  ))
}
if (n_available >= 8) {
  parallel_configs <- c(parallel_configs, list(
    list(parallel = TRUE, n_cores = 0)
  ))
}

results_par <- do.call(rbind, lapply(parallel_configs, function(cfg) {
  bench_fit(150, 80, parallel = cfg$parallel, n_cores = cfg$n_cores)
}))

results_par$time_per_iter <- results_par$elapsed / results_par$iterations
seq_time <- results_par$elapsed[1]
results_par$speedup <- seq_time / results_par$elapsed

knitr::kable(
  results_par[, c("n_cores", "iterations", "elapsed",
                   "time_per_iter", "speedup")],
  digits = 2,
  col.names = c("Cores", "Iterations", "Time (s)", "s/iter", "Speedup"),
  caption = "Parallel scaling (150 subjects, 80 measurements/subject)"
)
```

## 3. Visualization

```{r plot-size, fig.cap="Elapsed time by data size (sequential)"}
ggplot(results_size, aes(n_obs, elapsed)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Total Observations", y = "Elapsed Time (s)",
       title = "Sequential Performance") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r plot-parallel, fig.cap="Speedup by number of cores"}
ggplot(results_par, aes(factor(n_cores), speedup)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.5, fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  labs(x = "Number of Cores", y = "Speedup vs Sequential",
       title = "Parallel Speedup (150 subjects)") +
  theme_minimal()
```
